title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E02 — The Birth and Rise of Paris
Learning how Paris evolves from an ancient settlement to a Roman city and then the capital; studying medieval Paris through the Cluny Museum, the great cathedral of Notre Dame and the royal chapel of Sainte-Chapelle; following the growth of Paris.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E03 — The Splendor of Versailles
Discovering the Palace of Versailles as the world of Louis XIV; noting how the landscaping surrounding the palace symbolizes features of Louis's reign and how the Versailles court prizes royal spectacle; exploring Louis's patronage of the arts.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E04 — Paris in Revolution
Examining the social and political background of the French Revolution of 1789; visiting key locations in Paris where the events unfold, from a coffee house to the site of the Bastille prison and the Place de la Concorde; mapping Napoleon's rise.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E01 — How Washington DC Came to Be
Uncovering the origins of the District of Columbia; how the location for the national government is chosen; the original design and vision for the city by artist and engineer Pierre Charles L'Enfant; the creation and history of the National Mall.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E02 — The White House and the Presidency
Tracking the history and fortunes of the White House; visiting the White House, beginning with the Oval Office and Cabinet Room; visiting the parks adjoining the White House; the Jefferson and Franklin Delano Roosevelt memorials.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E03 — The Capitol Building and the Legislature
How the Capitol building is designed, constructed and expanded in the early years of the nation; touring the architectural and artistic wonders of the building; concluding with the House and Senate Chambers; the surrounding parks and gardens.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E04 — The Supreme Court and the Law of the Land
Studying the founding and history of the Supreme Court; touring this structure, its interior features, court facilities and artistic decoration; exploring the Court in action, which encompasses courtroom procedure and how cases are processed.

title: Cooking Across the Ages
description:
S01 E01 — Understanding Culture through Cooking
What one can learn about different cultural groups through the lens of their cookbooks; looking at two chicken recipes 200 years and a continent apart; learning to cook dishes from a 1748 French cookbook and "The Can-Opener Cookbook" of 1953.

title: Cooking Across the Ages
description:
S01 E02 — Ancient Rome: Cooking with Apicius
Whether the recipes in "De re coquinaria" are bizarre and disgusting, or they reflect a time of elegance and luxury; exploring its sala cattabia, minutal of apricots and botellum; finding three delicious, and even somewhat familiar, dishes.

title: Cooking Across the Ages
description:
S01 E03 — Imperial China: Soybeans and Dumplings
Examining the Chinese Wei dynasty's "Qi Min Yao Shu"; learning about Chinese agricultural practices going back to antiquity; the fermentation practices of the time; following a scaled-down recipe to create a fermented black bean dish.

title: Cooking Across the Ages
description:
S01 E04 — Medieval Egypt: Chickpeas and Phyllo Dough
Exploring recipes from 14th-century Egypt that reflect the interchange between the many cultures of the Eastern Mediterranean of the time; learning to make himmas kassa and a light and flaky phyllo dough stretched to the size of a table.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E01 — The Origins of Modern Archaeology
What archeologists actually do; the nature and scope of their work; misconceptions about the field; tracing the history of archeology, from its beginnings with the ancient Babylonian king Nabonidus to archeological luminaries of the 20th century.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E02 — Excavating Pompeii and Herculaneum
Traveling to the sites of Pompeii and Herculaneum, which are destroyed by the 79 A.D. eruption of Mount Vesuvius; the history of their excavation; the preservation of buildings, objects and human remains; discovering details of ancient Roman life.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E03 — Schliemann and His Successors at Troy
Following the exploits of Heinrich Schliemann as he looks for Homer's Troy; learning about his dig through nine stratified cities; the finds; the debates over which city is Troy; tracing subsequent work at the site; examining the conclusions.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E04 — Early Archaeology in Mesopotamia
The history of finds in Mesopotamia; the 19th-century unearthing of the Assyrian palaces at Nimrud and Nineveh, with their libraries of cuneiform texts; contemplating the 20th-century discovery of the treasures of the "Death Pits of Ur".

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E01 — Oscar Wilde's Decadent London
London when it is home to Oscar Wilde at the close of the 19th century; the details of Wilde's trial for indecency; the way London society is structured; how immense wealth and privilege, for some, leaves its imprint on the city and its history.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E02 — St. Paul's Cathedral in Faith, Fire, and Sin
St. Paul's Cathedral has overlooked London from a high point in the city for generations; the history of this church that has been much more than a place of worship; it has survived fire and the ravages of war; episodes from the cathedral's past.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E03 — Getting Blitzed at London's Café de Paris
An evening in March 1941, when the Café de Paris is destroyed in the Blitz; the history of the café; how its destruction reflects the horrors of wartime London; the resiliency of the citizens who keep calm and carry on under the threat of war.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E04 — On Carnaby Street during the Swinging '60s
Carnaby Street emerges in the 17th century; a symbol of social change in the 1960s; its history; it becomes a magnet for trendsetters and youth culture in post-war London; why these changes are embraced by some and seen as a threat by others.

title: In the Footsteps of Van Gogh
description:
S01 E01 — The World of Vincent Van Gogh
Tying together several facts about Van Gogh's life.

title: From Monet to Van Gogh: A History of Impressionism
description:
S01 E02 — Napoleon III's Paris
Napoleon III declares himself emperor of France in 1853; his aim is to modernize the economy of France, create a sophisticated rail-transport system and completely rebuild Paris; this means that, for most Parisians, life is utterly disrupted.

title: From Monet to Van Gogh: A History of Impressionism
description:
S01 E03 — Baudelaire and the Definition of Modernism
A poet and art critic named Charles Baudelaire begins writing systematically about art in 1846; his basic idea is that art should be "of its own times"; he struggles to find artists who will embody his ideals.

title: From Monet to Van Gogh: A History of Impressionism
description:
S01 E04 — The Shock of the New
Edouard Manet is among the best-educated and most authoritatively independent artists of the 19th century; he paints works that transcend Baudelaire; Manet's painting is as great as Baudelaire's poetry and greater than his art criticism.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E01 — Three Peoples Collide
Neither the Eurocentric term 'discovery' nor the blandly neutral 'encounters' do justice to the impact of Europeans, Africans and Native Americans coming together in the New World; a collision whose causes and effects are outlined in this lecture.

title: Conquest of the Americas
description:
S01 E02 — The Native Americans
Most of the inhabitants of the Americas arrive in migratory waves from Asia between 40,000 and 2,000 B.C.; their civilizations are based on sophisticated irrigation and farming; complex religions and social structures; rivaling those of Europe.

title: The Great Tours: Experiencing Medieval Europe
description:
S01 E01 — The Medieval City - A Feast for the Senses
The sights and smells of the medieval city; exploring the rich details of markets, monasteries, churches and religious and civic events; life in the townhouses of the rich, the tenements of the poor; the activities of medieval societies.

title: The Great Tours: Experiencing Medieval Europe
description:
S01 E02 — Rothenburg - Jewel On the Romantic Road
A well-preserved German medieval city; exploring the imposing mansions of the city's former elite, the grand fountains and the market square with its remarkable gothic town Hall; visiting St. Jakob's Church; walking the bastions of the city walls.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E01 — Native America: A Story of Survival
The commonly held views of Native Americans and the realities of a tapestry of vibrant cultures; Cobb explains the pitfalls that occur when history does not provide this crucial viewpoint; the mistake of consigning Native Americans to the past.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The Columbian Exchange: New Worlds for All
The misleading dichotomy of Old World and New World impacts perceptions of Native Americans; the Columbian Exchange is the crux behind the creation of new worlds for all; shaping everything from the fauna and flora to the cuisines of the world.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E01 — How Washington DC Came to Be
Uncovering the origins of the District of Columbia; how the location for the national government is chosen; the original design and vision for the city by artist and engineer Pierre Charles L'Enfant; the creation and history of the National Mall.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E02 — The White House and the Presidency
Tracking the history and fortunes of the White House; visiting the White House, beginning with the Oval Office and Cabinet Room; visiting the parks adjoining the White House; the Jefferson and Franklin Delano Roosevelt memorials.

title: Experiencing America: A Smithsonian Tour through American History
description:
S01 E01 — Star-Spangled Banner - Inspiring the Anthem
A tour of national treasures from the Smithsonian; the artifact that inspires the national anthem; the flag that flows over Fort McHenry when Francis Scott Key pens "The Star-Spangled Banner"; the battle for the fort and the history of the flag.

title: Experiencing America: A Smithsonian Tour through American History
description:
S01 E02 — Presidents and Generals - Images of Leadership
How some of the country's greatest leaders have seen themselves and been seen by the nation; Washington's uniform, swords and portraits; notable photographs of Lincoln; the history of Eisenhower's distinctive army jacket and his presidential look.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E01 — The Unknown Story of Ancient North America
Revealing the truths of ancient North America, which include pyramids, state-of-the-art highways and productive innovators; how the societies seemed destined to remain a mystery due to European conquerors and no written records.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The First Human Migrations to the Americas
DNA evidence pointing to Asia as the origin of all human migration to North America; migration passages across the Bering Strait; ancient habitation sites across the continent; why scientists cannot yet agree on the ages of the sites.

What one can learn about different cultural groups through the lens of their cookbooks; looking at two chicken recipes 200 years and a continent apart; learning to cook dishes from a 1748 French cookbook and "The Can-Opener Cookbook" of 1953.

title: Cooking Across the Ages
description:
S01 E02 — Ancient Rome: Cooking with Apicius
Whether the recipes in "De re coquinaria" are bizarre and disgusting, or they reflect a time of elegance and luxury; exploring its sala cattabia, minutal of apricots and botellum; finding three delicious, and even somewhat familiar, dishes.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E01 — The Unknown Story of Ancient North America
Revealing the truths of ancient North America, which include pyramids, state-of-the-art highways and productive innovators; how the societies seemed destined to remain a mystery due to European conquerors and no written records.

title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The First Human Migrations to the Americas
DNA evidence pointing to Asia as the origin of all human migration to North America; migration passages across the Bering Strait; ancient habitation sites across the continent; why scientists cannot yet agree on the ages of the sites.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E01 — Oscar Wilde's Decadent London
London when it is home to Oscar Wilde at the close of the 19th century; the details of Wilde's trial for indecency; the way London society is structured; how immense wealth and privilege, for some, leaves its imprint on the city and its history.

title: Notorious London: A City Tour
description:
S01 E02 — St. Paul's Cathedral in Faith, Fire, and Sin
St. Paul's Cathedral has overlooked London from a high point in the city for generations; the history of this church that has been much more than a place of worship; it has survived fire and the ravages of war; episodes from the cathedral's past.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E01 — The Historical Study of Christianity
The historical trajectory of Christianity; contemporary ignorance of its past; considering the value of the historical study of Christianity; looking at the methods and role of the historian; the sources and limitations of historical knowledge.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E02 — The First Cultural Context - Greece and Rome
Investigating the culture of the Mediterranean world in which Christianity is born; the legacy of Alexander; the features of Greek politics, religion and philosophy; learning about the nature of Roman rule and imperial order in the region.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E03 — The First Cultural Context - Judaism
The circumstances of Jewish life in ancient Palestine and the diaspora; examining cultural and ideological factors that divide the Jews; the tensions they face between assimilation and separation; their resistance to Greek culture and Roman rule.

title: The History of Christianity: From the Disciples to the Dawn of the Reformation
description:
S01 E04 — The Jesus Movement and the Birth of Christianity
Considering the resurrection as marking the birth of Christianity, as rooted in the claims of the first believers; assessing the contradiction between Jesus as the source of divine life and the degrading manner of his death.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E01 — Jesus - The Man Who Became God
The historical significance of the Christian belief in Jesus's divinity, in terms of its effects on Western civilization; learning about different scholarly views of the historical Jesus; tracing the diversity of early Christian thought.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E02 — Greco-Roman Gods Who Became Human
The accounts of divine mortals in the ancient world; the overlap between the human and divine worlds in Greco-Roman polytheistic religions; exploring three age-old models of divine men in both mythology and Christian scripture.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E03 — Humans as Gods in the Greco-Roman World
Delving into the interface between the human and the divine in pagan cultures; examining narratives describing people born of the sexual union of gods with mortals; looking at cases of humans who were exalted to the status of gods.

title: How Jesus Became God
description:
S01 E04 — Gods Who Were Human in Ancient Judaism
Accounts of divine humans and other godlike beings within ancient Judaism; exploring conceptions of divine beings that appear in human form in Genesis and Exodus; studying narratives of humans who become angelic beings in other Jewish texts.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E01 — The Birth of Christianity
This lecture introduces some issues essential to understanding how Christianity begins; growing away from its Jewish roots; ultimately becoming the most important religion of the civilization.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E02 — The Religious World of Early Christianity
This lecture introduces the pagan, polytheistic religions that dominate the early world; the most important Roman religion for the birth of Christianity; Judaism, the religion of Jesus and his followers.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E03 — The Historical Jesus
In the first of three lectures on the birth of Christianity, Professor Ehrman examines the life of Jesus of Nazareth; referred to both outside the New Testament and within the Gospels themselves.

title: From Jesus to Constantine: A History of Early Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Oral and Written Traditions about Jesus
How four anonymous authors who live decades after Jesus record traditions that have been circulating orally over the intervening years; examining the extent to which those traditions have been modified in the retelling.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E01 — The New Testament-An Overview
The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E03 — The Pauline Epistles
This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E04 — The Problem of Pseudonymity
This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E01 — Your Ancestry, Your Identity
Asking whether genes determine one's essential nature and identity, or one builds their own identity; exploring the essentialist and constructed philosophies; how one might incorporate aspects of both into their own view of personal identity.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E02 — What Genetic Testing Brings to Ancestry
Labs that provide DNA ancestry information use hundreds of thousands of ancestry-information markers, or AIMs; learning about the AIMs that relate to major identifiable lineages; what can be gleaned from mitochondrial DNA and Y-DNA.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E03 — Sensitive Approaches to Ancestry Results
There are many social issues affecting an individual's emotional response to receiving DNA ancestry results; how the reciprocal engagement method can help families face unexpected ancestry results; tips to consider before ordering one's own test.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E04 — When Family Narrative Meets Genetic Testing
People want a family narrative, whereas DNA just "wants" to move itself forward and is neutral on issues of race, subterfuge or social connection; how to create a strategic family narrative to incorporate the scientific facts of DNA ancestry results.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E05 — Privacy Versus Connection in DNA Testing
From the case of Henrietta Lacks to that of the Hagahai people of Papua New Guinea, scientists and government agencies have a history of bad actions with respect to biological samples; learning about the laws and programs in place to protect privacy.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E06 — The DNA Discussion Project Research
Learning about the DNA Discussion Project and its goals; current results regarding the ways in which DNA ancestry tests are changing identity; looking at questions about unanticipated results, sharing DNA ancestry results and social implications.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E07 — How Genograms Reveal Your Ancestry
A genogram is a graphic tool used to explore family history and relationships over a two- to three-generation period; discovering the powerful information that can be conveyed through a genogram as opposed to the traditional family tree diagram.

title: Identity in the Age of Ancestral DNA
description:
S01 E08 — Gaining Insight Through Your Genetics
Exploring the issue of birth assisted by reproductive technologies by meeting Maria, who learns as a teenager that she was born with the help of intrauterine insemination; considering how this knowledge affect an adolescent's identity.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E01 — Greeks and Macedonians
Philip II of Macedon sets the stage for the rise of his son, Alexander the Great, by conquering Greece; when Alexander invades the Persian territory of Asia Minor in 334 B.C., he embarks on the greatest career of conquest the world has ever seen.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E02 — Alexander the Divine?
After only two battles, Alexander commands more land than any Greek before him; he orders the Persian emperor to address him as an equal; at the height of his power, he visits Egypt, where he assumes the title of pharaoh and is hailed as a deity.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E03 — The Blazing Star
Whether his Egyptian sojourn convinces Alexander that he is a god or just teaches him the political value of blurring the lines between human and divine; how Alexander brings the Persian emperor to battle as he resumes his drive eastward.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E04 — Alexander-Myth and Reality
Alexander has an effect on the political development of the eastern Mediterranean; opinions about him remain deeply divided, both in antiquity and the current day; whether one can discern the historical Alexander, or the myth has swallowed the man.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E05 — The Formation of the Kingdoms
A generation of warfare among Alexander's successors splits his empire; after these "wars of the Diadochi", three major Hellenistic kingdoms emerge under the control of Alexander's former officers.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E06 — Egypt Under the Early Ptolemies
Ptolemy, one of Alexander's companions, transforms himself into a new pharaoh in Egypt even as he remains separate from the conquered Egyptians; how Ptolemy and his successors blend pharaonic and Macedonian practices to create a new kingdom.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E07 — Alexandria and the Library
Alexandria is the seat of Ptolemy's court; the city's library and museum are the premier cultural institutions of the Hellenistic world; whether Alexandria is a blend of Greek and Egyptian elements or the imposition of one culture over the other.

title: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic Age
description:
S01 E08 — The Seleucid Realm
The second great Hellenistic kingdom is ruled by the Seleucid dynasty, which builds cities from Syria to Iran; learning how the Seleucids rule a kingdom that stretches across all of Central Asia.
